subject.title: cron: systemEvent on main session silently ignores shell commands in payload text

question: Should OpenClaw land a heuristic cron CLI warning for shell-looking main-session systemEvent text, and should that warning direct users to --command or --command-argv now that command cron is shipped?
rationale: The implementation is small, but the warning is heuristic user-facing operator guidance and current command-cron semantics changed the best wording since the linked PR was opened.

options.title: Refresh and land command-cron guidance
options.body: Update the linked warning PR or a successor so add/edit warnings recommend --command or --command-argv, resolve conflicts, and keep runtime semantics unchanged.

options.title: Keep only docs-based guidance
options.body: Decline the CLI warning and rely on current cron docs, leaving shell-looking systemEvent payloads accepted without an inline warning.

options.title: Use stricter validation instead
options.body: Replace the non-blocking warning with a hard error or narrower validation rule, accepting a stronger compatibility and false-positive tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Refresh and land command-cron guidance
recommendation.body: Update the linked warning PR or a successor so add/edit warnings recommend --command or --command-argv, resolve conflicts, and keep runtime semantics unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc merged the command-cron path whose current behavior determines the right warning target and operator guidance.
